svg.title: How platelets stop bleeding
svg.desc: Four illustrated stages: injured endothelium exposes collagen; von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion and activation; fibrinogen bridges aggregate platelets; cross-linked fibrin reinforces the plug and traps red cells.

g.text: A damaged vessel is sealed by a platelet plug, then reinforced with fibrin.
Collagen is exposed beneath the endothelium.
A skin cut must reach a vessel to cause bleeding.
Platelets attach, change shape and release signals.
A fibrin mesh strengthens the initial plug.
Thrombin forms fibrin; factor XIII cross-links it.
Later: clot retraction → vessel repair → fibrinolysis (plasmin removes fibrin).
Schematic, not to scale. Stages overlap in vivo. Original educational artwork · Blood Lab
